title: Grandfather's Radio
passage:
On the highest shelf in my grandfather's sitting room stands an old wooden radio with a cracked dial and two brass knobs that have faded to a dull brown. For years I assumed it was simply a decoration, something too ancient and fragile to actually work.

One rainy evening, when the electricity in our neighborhood suddenly failed, Grandfather lifted the radio down carefully and fitted it with fresh batteries from the kitchen drawer. He turned the left knob slowly, and after a few seconds of crackling static, a clear voice began reading the evening news.

"This radio was my companion for forty years," he explained, settling into his favorite chair. He described how, as a young man working far from home, he had listened to it every night, waiting anxiously for news about the weather and the harvest in his village. Sometimes he heard recitations of the Quran or poetry programs, and he told me those broadcasts made the lonely nights feel shorter.

As he spoke, his eyes sparkled like a boy's, and I realized that the radio was not just a machine to him. It was a treasure box full of memories.

When the lights finally returned, I asked whether I could help him clean the radio and repair its cracked dial. Grandfather smiled warmly and said that nothing would make him happier.

questions.stem: Which word from the story is a noun?
options: slowly
companion
fragile
explained
questions.why: "Companion" names a person or thing; "slowly" is an adverb, "fragile" an adjective and "explained" a verb.

questions.stem: What is the plural form of "memory"?
options: memories
memorys
memoryes
memory's
questions.why: When a word ends in a consonant followed by y, change y to i and add -es: memories.

questions.stem: Who is the narrator of the story?
options: the grandfather's grandchild
the grandfather himself
a news reader on the radio
a neighbor in the village
questions.why: The narrator says "my grandfather's sitting room" and "I asked," so the story is told by the grandchild.

questions.stem: Why did Grandfather take the radio down from the shelf?
options: He wanted to sell it to a collector.
The narrator asked him to repair it.
Its brass knobs needed to be polished.
The electricity in the neighborhood had failed.
questions.why: The second paragraph says he lifted it down on a rainy evening when the electricity failed.

questions.stem: How did the narrator's view of the radio change during the story?
options: From a useful tool to a broken toy
From a family secret to a school project
From a mere decoration to a treasure of memories
From a gift for Grandfather to a gift for a neighbor
questions.why: At first the narrator thought it was just a decoration; later the narrator saw it as "a treasure box full of memories."

questions.stem: The narrator says Grandfather's "eyes sparkled like a boy's." What does this comparison show?
options: He was having trouble seeing in the dark.
He was crying because the radio was broken.
He was angry that the electricity had failed.
He felt young and excited as he remembered.
questions.why: This simile shows the joy and youthful excitement that the memories brought him.

questions.stem: Which event in the story could really happen?
options: A radio plays a man's own memories aloud.
A radio restores the electricity in a neighborhood.
An old radio works again after new batteries are added.
A radio's dial repairs its own crack overnight.
questions.why: Old battery radios can work again with fresh batteries; the other events are imaginary.

questions.stem: Which feeling is MOST present in the story?
options: fear of storms and darkness
warm affection between a grandchild and a grandparent
jealousy about an expensive gift
anger at a broken machine
questions.why: The shared memories, Grandfather's warm smile and the offer to help all show affection between them.

questions.stem: Which information does the story leave LEAST clear?
options: What the radio was made of
Where Grandfather was working when he was young
What the voice on the radio read
What the narrator offered to do at the end
questions.why: The story says he worked "far from home" but never tells us where; the other details are stated.

questions.stem: Which title BEST describes the events of the story?
options: A Storm Destroys the Village
How to Build a New Radio
The Narrator's First Day at Work
The Voice on Grandfather's Shelf
questions.why: The story centers on Grandfather's old radio and the memories it carries.
